guidelines.title: Acute Coronary Syndrome & Chest Pain Clinical Guidelines

reference_standards.hs_troponin_i: <14 ng/L (Normal threshold; >14 indicates acute myocardial necrosis)

guidelines.clinical_guidance: Substernal chest pressure radiating to the arm/jaw with diaphoresis requires immediate emergency ECG and cardiac biomarker evaluation. Do not reassure without physician evaluation.

guidelines.title: Glycemic Markers & Diabetes Management Guidelines

reference_standards.fasting_glucose: 70-99 mg/dL (Normal), 100-125 mg/dL (Impaired fasting glucose), >=126 mg/dL (Diabetes threshold)

guidelines.clinical_guidance: Fasting glucose >126 mg/dL or HbA1c >=6.5% requires confirmatory testing and clinical correlation. Extreme glucose (>300 mg/dL with ketones) requires urgent metabolic evaluation.

guidelines.title: Complete Blood Count & Anemia Evaluation Standards
guidelines.clinical_guidance: Hemoglobin <12.0 g/dL in women or <13.5 g/dL in men indicates anemia; ferritin and iron studies are indicated to evaluate microcytic hypochromic patterns.

guidelines.title: Renal Function & Glomerular Filtration Standards
guidelines.clinical_guidance: Elevated serum creatinine with reduced eGFR (<60 mL/min) warrants assessment of hydration status, nephrotoxic medications, and chronic renal parameters.

guidelines.title: Thyroid Function Testing Guidelines
guidelines.clinical_guidance: Elevated TSH (>4.0 uIU/mL) with low Free T4 indicates primary hypothyroidism; low TSH (<0.4 uIU/mL) with elevated Free T4 indicates hyperthyroidism.

guidelines.title: Hepatic Transaminases & Liver Panel Guidelines
guidelines.clinical_guidance: Transaminase elevations (ALT > AST) suggest hepatocellular inflammation or parenchymal stress; total bilirubin >1.5 mg/dL warrants cholestatic evaluation.

guidelines.title: Serum Electrolytes & Panic Thresholds
guidelines.clinical_guidance: Potassium >6.0 mEq/L represents severe hyperkalemia with arrhythmia risk; urgent clinical and ECG monitoring required.
